objective: Extend ticket A's theorem from four rings to n >= 3 rings of s >= 4 cells: every ring on rule 60 or 102, every middle ring's contacts two apart, c1 reading its partners and each later contact both neighbours on its first ring and its partner on its second. Prove that every contact persists and the last contact binds the first ring exactly when C(T - (n - 1), e) is odd, e the sum of k_j - 1 over the middle rings after mirroring.
status: Proved 2026-11-08 (by hand from ticket A's lemmas; finite claims checked): for n >= 3 rings of s >= 4 cells with rule 60 or 102 on each ring and every middle ring's contacts two apart, every contact persists and the last contact binds the first ring exactly when C(T - (n - 1), e) is odd, e the sum of k_j - 1 after mirroring: composition at recurring lags at every length and ring size, at every lag never.
title: One-sided additive paths of every length
